finding: | `kits/language/javascript/manifest.toml:269-273` `tools.eslint.import_style` default `{"**/*" = "js"}` | The `.js` suffix fits only compiled Node.js ESM. Only the nextjs kit sets `extensionless`. Vite, React, Vue, Svelte, Astro, and React Native apps get every relative import reported at level `all` (`gspot/import-style`). | Default from the scope's tsconfig `moduleResolution`: `bundler` gives `extensionless`, `node16` and `nodenext` give `js`. Or have each bundler framework kit set `extensionless`. |

section: Kits: JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, and Markdown
finding: | `kits/language/javascript/eslint.config.mjs.tmpl:96-143,177-222,315-317` duplicated rules | One defect is reported by two or three rules. The template's own comment (line 147) says this is wrong: "two owners would give two answers". The duplicates: `no-unused-vars` or `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` plus `sonarjs/no-unused-vars` and `sonarjs/unused-import`; `regexp/no-super-linear-backtracking`, `security/detect-unsafe-regex`, and `sonarjs/slow-regex`; `no-empty-character-class`, `regexp/no-empty-character-class`, and `sonarjs/no-empty-character-class`; `security/detect-eval-with-expression` and `sonarjs/code-eval`; `no-param-reassign` and `sonarjs/no-parameter-reassignment`; `no-useless-catch` and `sonarjs/no-useless-catch`; `unicorn/no-lonely-if` and `sonarjs/no-collapsible-if`; `for-direction` and `sonarjs/for-loop-increment-sign`; `n/no-deprecated-api` and `security/detect-new-buffer`; `@typescript-eslint/no-deprecated` and `sonarjs/deprecation`. All of them are on in the presets or the template (verified). | Keep one rule for each defect and turn the others off. Where a core, regexp, n, or typescript-eslint rule exists, keep that one, because it gives the most precise report. |
verification: Batch 69 partially resolves three duplicate families with pinned native source and regression evidence. Keep this record open for the other listed overlaps. Partial implementation of finding 022: retain regexp/no-empty-character-class as the sole owner of empty and impossible character classes, core no-useless-catch for redundant rethrows, and sonarjs/no-collapsible-if for nested conditions. Disable only core and Sonar empty-character-class rules, Sonar useless-catch, and Unicorn no-lonely-if. Preserve both coverage levels, every plugin pin and project prerequisite. No opt-in check control or additional selection mechanism is introduced. /tmp/gspot-native-overlap-equivalence-proof.json compares the complete actual configuration in 36 native JavaScript, TypeScript, framework, test, script and extensionless Node contexts. Only the four disabled duplicate owners change; every other rule, setting, registered plugin, parser metadata, global and linter option is identical. Native initial cases pass with 34 assertions (4.73 seconds). The exact final cases against the old production template both fail on duplicate-rule ownership, /tmp/gspot-native-overlap-baseline-proof.json (2.69 seconds); restore every production byte afterward.

Batch 70 partially resolves unused-binding/import, dynamic-execution and Buffer-constructor duplicates. Keep this aggregate record open for regex performance, parameter mutation, loop direction and typed deprecation. Partially continue finding 022: core no-unused-vars owns JavaScript bindings/imports and @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars owns typed bindings/imports. Disable sonarjs/no-unused-vars and sonarjs/unused-import in the shared JavaScript template; delete the now-redundant TypeScript off override. Preserve every existing underscore, destructuring, parameter and disposal option, JSDoc type handling, scope and native project prerequisite. Disable security/detect-eval-with-expression and security/detect-new-buffer; retain sonarjs/code-eval and n/no-deprecated-api as their broader native owners. Keep all genuine detection enabled at both levels, all pins unchanged, and introduce no opt-in control, new setting or additional selection strategy. /tmp/gspot-native-bindings-equivalence-proof.json compares every rule, setting, plugin, linter option and language option across 36 actual native contexts at both levels. Only the four disabled duplicate owners change; all other configuration remains identical. The exact final four cases against both previous production assets yield two earlier controls passing and two intended new failures, baseline-proof.json (7.21 seconds); restore every current byte afterward. No unrelated failure counts as regression evidence.

Batch 73 partially resolves regex-performance and typed-deprecation overlaps in finding 022. Keep this aggregate record open for parameter mutation and loop direction. Keep regexp/no-super-linear-backtracking as the sole regex performance owner; disable sonarjs/slow-regex and security/detect-unsafe-regex at both levels. Keep @typescript-eslint/no-deprecated as the sole typed deprecated-API owner; disable sonarjs/deprecation only in the TypeScript fragment, including typed framework source. JavaScript retains Sonar deprecation. Preserve all pins, genuine project prerequisites, every other native rule and manual configuration overrides; add no opt-in control, setting or coverage choice. The 36-context native comparison changes only these three duplicate owners: the two regex rules in 36 contexts and typed deprecation in 20. Every other rule, parser, plugin, global, setting and linter option remains identical. /tmp/gspot-native-semantic-equivalence-proof.json retains proof. Pinned regexp 3.3.0 detects exponential and polynomial backtracking through literals, string constructors and static templates; bounded and delimiter-separated nested repetition and Unicode sets are accepted. The old security heuristic reports the tested safe bounded and delimiter-separated patterns. Native TypeScript ownership reports actual deprecated calls, aliases, classes, computed and ordinary properties, type references and deprecated overloads. It omits the separate import-binding warnings that Sonar also emitted; this is a deliberate diagnostic change, not equality of every old message. Current overloads and current API uses remain accepted. Native initial cases pass eight tests with 134 assertions in 20.47 seconds. Exact final cases against both old production assets yield four existing controls passing and all four intended new failures (16.43 seconds). /tmp/gspot-native-semantic-baseline-proof.json confirms restoration of every current source byte. Native loop and parameter probes prove unique detection by both existing owners; retain them while their remaining overlap is unresolved.

section: Kits: JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, and Markdown
finding: | `kits/language/javascript/eslint.config.mjs.tmpl:178,183,187` security rules | `detect-buffer-noassert` looks for an argument that Node.js 10 removed, and the default Node.js floor is 22. `detect-no-csrf-before-method-override` checks the order of Express middleware in every JavaScript project. `detect-possible-timing-attacks` is on at level `recommended` and reports every `if` that compares an identifier named exactly `token`, `auth`, `secret`, `password`, `pass`, `hash`, or `api`, including `if (token === undefined)` (verified in the rule source). | Delete the first rule. Move the second to the express kit. Delete the third, or move it to level `all`. |

section: Kits: JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, and Markdown
finding: | `kits/language/javascript/eslint.config.mjs.tmpl:316`, `src/config/generation/eslint-levels.json:897,932-933,967,1029,1031` | The full sonarjs preset (279 rules) is applied. At level `recommended` it reports ordinary code: every `spawn('git')` (`no-os-command-from-path`), every `Math.random()` (`pseudo-random`), plain `http://` URLs (`no-clear-text-protocols`), and `/tmp` (`publicly-writable-directories`). Meanwhile the general `security/detect-child-process` is only at level `all`. `no-hardcoded-passwords` and `no-hardcoded-secrets` duplicate the secrets kit. | Move the first four to level `all`. Turn off the two secret rules, because the secrets kit owns secret detection. |
